question: Which Mughal emperor led a campaign against Kashmir, and in which year did it took place?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Akbar, 1586**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Akbar**, the third Mughal emperor, launched a campaign against **Kashmir** in the year **1586** to expand the Mughal Empire and secure control over the northern frontiers.
 
• The campaign was a part of Akbar's broader strategy of territorial expansion, which aimed to consolidate the Mughal Empire in India.
 
• Before Akbar's campaign, Kashmir was ruled by independent local rulers. By 1586, after significant resistance, Akbar annexed Kashmir into the Mughal Empire.
 
• Akbar's governance style ensured that Kashmir became a prosperous region, and it was integrated into the empire's administration under the Mansabdari system.
 
• This campaign was significant not only for territorial consolidation but also for ensuring the political and economic stability of the northern regions of the empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Babur:**

 
 
• **Babur** was the founder of the Mughal Empire, ruling between **1526-1530**. He was known for his victories, such as the First Battle of Panipat (1526), but there is no historical record of him campaigning against Kashmir.
 
 
 
• **Humayun:**
 
 
• **Humayun**, Akbar's father, ruled from **1530-1556** (with interruptions). His reign was marked by struggles against Sher Shah Suri, and he did not launch any campaigns against Kashmir.
 
 
 
• **Akbar:**
 
 
• **Akbar's reign** (1556-1605) was notable for his military conquests, administrative reforms, and promotion of cultural integration.
 
• In **1586**, Akbar annexed Kashmir, recognizing its strategic and economic importance. This region was later known for its contribution to art, culture, and trade in the Mughal Empire.
 
 
 
• **Jahangir:**
 
 
• **Jahangir**, Akbar's successor, ruled from **1605-1627**. While he is remembered for his love of Kashmir and frequent visits there, he did not lead a campaign to conquer it, as it was already a part of the empire.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kashmir under Mughals:** After Akbar's annexation, Kashmir became a vital part of the Mughal Empire, known for its natural beauty and contribution to the empire's economy.
 
• **Akbar's Mansabdari System:** This administrative reform allowed efficient governance of vast territories, including newly annexed regions like Kashmir.
 
• **Integration Policies:** Akbar's policies focused on integrating diverse regions under one central authority, ensuring political stability and cultural harmony.
